rationale.conceptual: The method is an established non-trivial DFT+U+SO approach; it requires correctly setting up all-in/all-out non-collinear magnetism, computing gaps and magnetic moments, and fitting a spin model from constrained energies. This is more than a minor variation but not a novel algorithm.
rationale.execution: The workflow has around 4-6 stages: many SCF runs (16 for phase diagram), post-processing to extract gaps, constrained DFT for anisotropy, and DOS computation. There are dependencies between steps, and the DFT tooling (plane-wave code, pseudopotentials, non-collinear setup) adds orchestration complexity.

difficulty.reasoning: The paper uses standard LSDA+SO+U DFT, a well-established method, but implementing the correct magnetic ordering, constrained spin rotations, and extracting gaps and model parameters requires careful understanding of non-collinear magnetism and DFT specifics. The pipeline involves multiple SCF runs across Ueff values and spin configurations, plus constrained calculations and post-processing, amounting to a moderate multi-stage orchestration.

compute_estimate.reasoning: DFT on a 22-atom primitive cell with 12x12x12 k-mesh and full spin-orbit coupling is CPU-bound; each run uses a few GB RAM, negligible input data.
